frame_metadata.gps_note: First take with GPS on every frame. App frames carry a 9-key GPS block written by the F0 build; stock-camera HEICs carry Apple's full 15-key block. Both bind the frame to the Met to within a few metres.

source_note: App frames are camera-roll copies (Image Capture over USB) bound to the manifest by capture time with tools/manifest/bind-frames.py — see derived/2026-09-20-met-frames.json.

expected.title: Jasper lentoid: Two waterfowl
expected.title_note: The card writes the material and form on one line and the subject on the next, joined by a colon. The API title is just 'Jasper Lentoid'.
expected.date_edtf_note: BCE years are astronomical: 375 BCE is -0374. Ranges are intervals; '~' marks each end when the label says 'ca.'. A named span like 'late 6th century' is written as the conventional interval and noted in date_raw.

differ.title: label adds the subject line 'Two waterfowl'
differ.era_notation: this card says BCE; the Greek and Roman cards two galleries away say B.C.

traps.neighbours_bleed_in: Two other cards are partly in frame at the bottom — 'Agate lentoid: Lion attacking goa…' and '…rd and woman'. Mac OCR flagged 4 of 10 lines as truncated; those are the neighbours, not this card. A reader has to pick the card that is whole, and the app's screen-aspect crop makes the bleed more likely, not less.
traps.work_is_two_objects: The seal and its modern impression are displayed as a pair; the work frame shows two things per accession. Pairing tests (D15) should expect this in any gem gallery.
